environment.description: Same application deployed behind CloudFront distribution with a Lambda@Edge viewer-response function (ARN: arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:XXXX:function:csp-enforcer:7) that appends response headers. The function injects a Content-Security-Policy header with directive `script-src 'self' https://cdn.example.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'` on all text/html responses. The distribution behavior pattern '/*' has this trigger attached at viewer-response phase. Note: the CSP does NOT use 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval'. Additionally, MongoDB is configured with JSON Schema validation on the 'devices' collection that restricts `displayWidget` to type string with maxLength 0 (effectively disabling the field) via db.runCommand({collMod: 'devices', validator: {$jsonSchema: {properties: {displayWidget: {bsonType: 'string', maxLength: 0}}}}}) with validationAction 'error'.

config.runtime: Node.js 18 on ECS Fargate behind CloudFront
config.cdn: CloudFront distribution d-XXXXX with Lambda@Edge viewer-response trigger
config.lambda_edge_function: csp-enforcer:7 - adds CSP header: script-src 'self' https://cdn.example.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'
config.database: MongoDB 6.0 with JSON Schema validator on 'devices' collection, displayWidget field constrained to maxLength: 0 with validationAction: error
config.network: Private subnet, CloudFront origin-only access via custom header verification
